full_suite_analysis.verdict: no regression introduced by this change
evidence: No DEV-2486 test (GlKits*, OrgKitCameraNames*) failed in ANY run.

The failure SET churns between identical-code runs — 16 problems on a pressured ClickHouse, 5 on a restarted one, with DIFFERENT names each time. That churn is the signature of shared-state flakiness, not a regression.

ClickHouse container memory pressure is a confirmed amplifier: restarting clarity-qa-clickhouse (3.70 GiB -> 2.17 GiB of 5.79 GiB) took the HEAD full suite from 16 problems to 5 — fewer than BASE's 6, which was itself measured under pressure. This is the documented failure mode in the clarity/testing knowledge card (error 241 raised inside RequiresClickhouse's TRUNCATE setup, before any test logic, presenting as a batch of unrelated failures).
Isolated-class comparison HEAD vs BASE over every implicated class (180 tests): HEAD's failure set is a strict SUBSET of BASE's. Nothing failed at HEAD that did not also fail at BASE.

The two names unique to the clean HEAD run (HitDirectHotspotQueryTest::test_resolves_latest_hotlist_version_on_status_transition, DashboardCardExpansionTest::test_dispatching_dashboard_toggle_card_expands_the_matching_chart) both PASS in isolation at HEAD (24/24) and neither file references any DEV-2486 symbol.
The 4 stable failures (CloseInactiveShiftsCommandTest x2, EnsureOpenShiftTest, ScoutUsersResourceTest risky) reproduce identically at BASE.
full_suite_analysis.caveat: The local literal clarity/zod ClickHouse databases are SHARED across worktrees, so another session running tests concurrently perturbs any full-suite result here. CI runs an isolated ClickHouse service and is the authoritative signal.
full_suite_analysis.concurrency_confirmation: CONFIRMED at BASE under identical conditions. Two peer sessions were active on this machine and the literal clarity/zod ClickHouse databases are SHARED across worktrees. clarity.hotlist was observed holding 3 foreign rows mid-run. HasStatDrillDownTest run ALONE fails at d5a07d19 as well (2 failures) as it does at HEAD (1 error + 2 failures) — seconds apart, same live concurrent writer. Four independent confirmations in total: (1) no DEV-2486 test ever failed in any run, (2) the failure set churns names between identical-code runs, (3) restarting the container took HEAD from 16 problems to 5, (4) the implicated classes fail at BASE too when run alone. CI's isolated ClickHouse service is the authoritative signal.
